firstPass.prompt: Precise sprite pose edit for an original isometric zombie game. Image 1 is the exact existing approved design to edit. Keep the two isolated full-body views of the SAME character, one in each half: on left keep the 3/4 front view pointing screen-right and toward camera (SE); on right keep the 3/4 back view pointing screen-right and away (NE). Camera looking down at same angle as reference, no change to side or viewing direction. Preserve character identity, clothes, colors, paired tears, center stains, pixel art with muted clustered shading, scale proportions and lighting. Redraw the idle pose in BOTH views consistently in character space: Broad adult work-jacket man. Anatomical RIGHT shoulder dropped conspicuously; head lolls toward right shoulder, not just looking sideways. His weight is on the flat LEFT boot under him. The unweighted RIGHT boot trails behind on its toe, heel clearly raised; leave readable space between boots. Arms hang slack. Stance should read lopsided instantly when downscaled to 48 pixels tall. No other edits. Keep enough empty space between poses and around edges, full bodies including boots, genuine transparent background, no shadows, text or floor. Wide horizontal two-cell sprite sheet.

rearRevision.prompt: Precisely edit the pose of the figure in the RIGHT half only of this original pixel art sprite sheet. Keep the left half and the genuine transparent canvas unchanged. In the right half, keep the exact original character, outfit, textures, muted colors, scale, and its elevated 3/4 back view aimed toward the upper-right. Change weight distribution, following absolute screen directions exactly. The screen-LEFT boot (left half of this rear-view silhouette) is the flat weighted boot underneath the hip, entire sole flat, heel down, leg straighter. The screen-RIGHT boot touches just the TOE, with heel visibly higher and calf bent back, displaced slightly outward to screen-right so both boots read distinctly. The screen-right shoulder and head remain dropped to screen-right. Keep both full bodies fully inside the canvas with plenty of margin, no props, shadows or text.
